free_tier.stated: "Research projects that are new to NERSC and/or HPC may apply for small Exploratory awards, up to 250 node hours". Exploratory requests are accepted at any time, decided within four weeks of applying, and last 18 months. A Perlmutter CPU node is 2 AMD EPYC 7763 processors totalling 128 cores and 512 GB of memory, so 250 node-hours is 32,000 core-hours. The NERSC Director's Reserve, the other discretionary pool, is explicitly "not generally open to the public" and needs "prior arrangements with NERSC".

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
chaining: This is the clearest case in the file where the identity instrument is named rather than implied: an ORCID iD and an email get the account, and the Institutional User Agreement is the single document that stands between an unaffiliated person and 32,000 core-hours, so it composes only with an organisation willing to sign with Berkeley Lab.

limits.value: An Institutional User Agreement between Berkeley Lab and the PI's sponsoring organisation is required when the project is not federally (US) funded, so an unaffiliated applicant needs an organisation willing to sign a contract with a US national laboratory before any of the 32,000 core-hours exist.

notes: The finding worth carrying is the refutation: NERSC's Director's Reserve is widely described as an open door and the vendor page says the opposite in one sentence, while the Exploratory award is the real small route and needs an agreement rather than a review panel. Foreign nationals are permitted under the appropriate use policy except in embargoed countries and on restricted party lists, which is a separate gate from the funding one.
